title: Day 1 of AI/Algo Trading (Paper) - Posting for accountability
author: Enzobevmax
selftext:
Day 1 in the books! Hoping to keep similar format for each day. Trying to add in quick facts to answer easy, repetitive questions.

I will also post descriptions of the top two performing setups for that day, for now, in picture form as we are all looking for more setups(myself included!) and I'm happy to share what I have.

**After today** I will be using a slightly different picture format to deliver the same information, Claude will auto-generate this for me. Just easier!

Thanks for all the feedback, support, and camaraderie!

**Today:** \[+$674\] across 5 day-trading accounts · Primary \[-$81\] · green streak \[0\]  
Best setup: \[Morning Momentum Pop, +$650\] (details in pic)

**Quick facts -** To hopefully answer quick questions

* **AI:** Claude (Opus 5.5) builds, tests and runs it
* **Broker:** Alpaca API, paper trading
* **Setups:** 108 (Currently) live, built on basic indicators (RSI, VWAP, volume / buy-sell pressure, gaps, opening range, prior-day highs and lows, ATR)
* **Setup Generator:** a bot that invents 10 new setups a night from those same indicators and trades them on its own paper account

Setup Life cycle

    Idea / Generator
     └─ 2-yr backtest (costs in)
         └─ Replay on real sessions
             └─ Testing 1 / 2 / Generator (paper)
                 └─ Primary (paper)
                     └─ Live $ (after a green streak)
    Losers: Primary → Testing → Graveyard

Stats Description

* **Avg R:** average profit per trade, in units of the risk taken. Costs, fees and slippage are already in. +0.5R = earns half its risk per trade.
* **Break-even win rate:** the win rate a setup needs just to not lose money. Beat it and you’re profitable.
* **Confidence (t):** how sure we are it isn’t luck. 2+ is solid; under 1 could be luck.

Fun stuff!

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: With 108 live setups plus 10 new ones generated nightly, a fixed t-stat threshold of 2 will produce plenty of apparent winners by chance. I’d make promotion depend on a multiple-testing correction or false-discovery estimate that includes every generated and graveyard setup, not just survivors. Also define the “green streak” before observing it and require Primary to pass on sessions that were unavailable to Claude Opus 5.5 when the setup was created. Today’s +$674 is almost entirely the +$650 Morning Momentum Pop while Primary lost $81, so reporting account-level exposure and setup overlap would show whether those five accounts represent independent evidence. The picture is unavailable here, so its trade count and Avg R cannot be checked.

comments.author: Signal_Pace_7968
comments.body: One thing that jumps out on the account cards: since start, Primary, Testing 1, Testing 2 and Graveyard are all red, and the only green one is the Setup Generator, which trades brand new setups with no promotion at all. Different start dates, so not a fair comparison yet. But if it holds, the promotion step isn’t adding anything over just trading fresh random setups. Might be worth keeping the generator as your baseline on purpose and judging Primary against it, not against zero.

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body: Interesting thought. I need that kind of input on how to structure things in the future. I'm just super cautious on the generator setups now. Like, they are doing well but I know that could just be fluff given how little "playing time" they've gotten. Thank you!

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Thanks for posting the daily numbers, and for labeling the generated setups as not tested edges. One thing to watch is that "best setup of the day" is picked after the results are in, so with 60 or more new generated setups, some will top the list by luck each day. A fairer way is to post the same fixed list each day and follow each setup's record over many sessions, then show the ones that keep holding up. The top setup also only trades on broad up mornings, so it fires on few days, and a small number of trades can't tell skill from luck yet. Cymetica's Backtest Labs is another place to test a setup against history before it joins a live list.

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body:
Very good point. I might just say, top 2 not from generator. You're right, it isn't fair to put lucky ones in which will be a bulk of them.

Maybe on another post I'll provide some insight on the diversity of our other setups. It'll shed more light on the specifics and uniqueness of each one based on ao many factors, one of which being time of day.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Good to hear, and posting the top two from the non-generated setups is a fairer list. A breakdown by time of day would be useful too, since a setup that only works in one window of the day can be sized for that window. Thanks for being open to the feedback.

comments.author: QATSAlgo
comments.body:
Alongside setup-level results, I’d keep one timestamped account-level equity/exposure trace. Several setups can express the same bet, so individually acceptable trades can create an unacceptable combined drawdown. Before promotion, replay the exact daily-reset and loss-limit policy as well as costs, and freeze the promotion criteria before seeing the streak.



We’re QATS. If you ever want to try a separate perpetuals-prop branch of the experiment, our Trading API exposes market data, account/risk state, orders and positions: [https://quantityproject.github.io/qats-trader-api/](https://quantityproject.github.io/qats-trader-api/) . It needs a dedicated adapter; it is not an Alpaca-compatible stock API. Evaluations and initial funded accounts are simulated, under published plan rules; neither a green streak nor an API connection proves an edge.
